title: Clinical Microfluidic Chip Platform for the Isolation of Versatile Circulating Tumor Cells
protocol: Culture the tumor cells MCF-7, MDA-MB-231, and HeLa for determining the capture efficiency.
Dilute the tumor cell suspension in PBS.
Count the number of tumor cells in the suspension.
Repeat dilution and counting until 100 tumor cells per 1 mL of PBS are obtained.

Culture the cells in a cell culture flask with a starting cell number of ~ 1 x 10^5 cells in 1 mL of Dulbecco's modified Eagle's medium (DMEM) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1% penicillin-streptomycin.
Incubate the culture flask in a humidified atmosphere at 37 °C with a 5% CO2 atmosphere until cells grow to 95% confluence.
Detach cells from the culture dishes with 0.25% trypsin solution for 2 min.
Stain the tumor cells with calcein AM by adding 3 µL of calcein AM to the culture dish and incubating in the incubator for 30 min.
Count the cultured tumor cells in PBS using a cell counting chamber.
Dilute the stained cells until 100 tumor cells per 1 mL of PBS are obtained.
Take 50 µL of cell suspension to count the number of tumor cells under a microscope.
Decide the volume needed to obtain 100 tumor cells based on the initial count.
Introduce a cell suspension containing 100 tumor cells per 1 mL PBS into the microfluidic chip using a syringe pump at flow rates of 0.5 mL/h, 1 mL/h, 2 mL/h, 3 mL/h, 4 mL/h, and 5 mL/h.
Count the number of captured and flowing out tumor cells for each flow rate.
Calculate capture efficiency as (Number of cells captured / (Number of cells captured + Number of cells flowing out)) × 100%.
Repeat the process with different numbers of tumor cells from 10 to 100.
Inject sample suspensions containing 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 tumor cells diluted in 1 mL PBS into microfluidic chips using a hollow needle.
Detect and enumerate the number of captured tumor cells for each sample.
Stain tumor cells with calcein AM.
Enumerate 100 tumor cells in 5 μL of PBS.
Spike these cells into 1 mL of whole normal blood samples.
Introduce spiked samples into the chip.
Enumerate the number of tumor cells captured on the chip using green immunofluorescence.
Calculate capture efficiency after enumeration.
Repeat steps for nine additional concentrations of tumor cell numbers from 10 to 90.
Enumerate 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 tumor cells without staining.
Spike enumerated cells into 1 mL of whole normal blood samples.
Introduce these samples into the microfluidic chip for capture.
Stain captured tumor cells on the chip with Hoechst, CK-FITC, and CD45-PE.
Mix fluorescent dye solution by putting 3-5 μL of fluorescent dye into 20-30 μL of PBS.
Introduce stained solution onto the microfluidic chip using a syringe.
Enumerate tumor cells captured on the chip with both blue and green immunofluorescence to determine capture efficiency.
Modify the microfluidic chip for affinity-based capture of anti-EpCAM.
Modify the surface of the chip with 100 μL of 4% (v/v) 3-mercaptopropyl trimethoxysilane in ethanol at room temperature for 45 min.
Wash the chip with ethanol 3 times.
Add 100 µL of N-ε-maleimidobutyryloxy succinimide ester (GMBS, 1 µM) onto the chip and allow it to interact for 30 min.
Wash the chip with PBS 3 times.
Introduce 1 mL of PBS onto the chip to wash.
Treat the chip with 30-40 µL of 10 µg/mL neutravidin at room temperature for 30 min, leading to immobilization of the cells onto the GMBS.
Flush the excess avidin from the chip with PBS.
Modify the chip with 3 µL of anti-biotinylated EpCAM antibody at a concentration of 10 µg/mL in 100 µL of PBS with 1% (w/v) BSA.
Keep this modification overnight.
Re-process clinical cancer patient blood samples using red blood cells lysis solution.
Introduce 2-3 mL of blood sample directly onto the microfluidic chip using a syringe.
Add 6-9 mL of RBS lysis solution into 2-3 mL of blood.
Centrifuge at 111 x g for 5-8 min at room temperature.
Discard the upper layer of red clear liquid after centrifugation.
Capture cells on the chip as described in step 1.
Stain the chip for CTCs captured using Hoechst, CK-FITC, and CD45-PE.
Add 3 µL of CK-FITC to 20 µL of PBS.
Introduce diluted CK-FITC onto the chip.
Allow staining with CK-FITC for 30 min.
Introduce 300 µL of PBS onto the chip to wash the chip.
Add 3 µL of CD45-PE to 20 µL of PBS.
Introduce diluted CD45-PE onto the chip.
Allow standing with CD45-PE for 30 min.
Introduce 300 µL of PBS onto the chip to wash the chip.
Identify CTCs with an inverted fluorescence microscope at 20x or 40x magnification.
Enumerate CTCs as Hoechst+/CK-FITC+/CD45− and WBCs as Hoechst+/CK-FITC−/CD45+.
Enrich the captured CTCs by flushing with PBS through a syringe in the reverse direction onto the microfluidic chip from the outlet to the inlet.
Repeat the washing step 3 times using 1 mL of PBS for each wash.
Stain the tumor cells or CTCs captured on the microfluidic chip using calcein AM.
Add 5 µL of calcein AM to 20 µL of PBS and stain the cells for 30 min.
Centrifuge at 111 x g for 2 min at room temperature to obtain tumor cells, then suspend in 1 mL of PBS.

Pass through 20 µL of DAPI solution (10 µL of DAPI reagent in 20 µL of PBS) at the optimal flow rate of 1 mL/h for big-ellipse microfilters and 1.5 mL/h for trapezoid ones to identify cellular nuclei.
Pass through 20 µL of anti-cytokeratin stock solution (3 µL of anti-cytokeratin antibody in 20 µL of PBS) to react with the chip for 30 min.
Stain WBCs captured on the chip with 25 μL of anti-CD45 antibody solution (5 μL of anti-CD45 in 20 μL of PBS).
Allow staining for 30 min.
Wash the chip with PBS.
Identify epithelial cells emitting both blue and green fluorescence.
Use a fluorescence microscope to excite the sample with a blue laser.
Find cells emitting blue fluorescence (nucleate cells) at magnifications of 10x, 20x, or 40x.
Select a clear field for tumor cell identification.
For the blue laser source, use an excitation wavelength of 420-485 nm and an emission wavelength of 515 nm.
Use another laser source without moving the samples.
Rotate the fluorescence microscope and excite the sample with the green laser.
Find cells emitting green fluorescence, indicative of tumor cells.
Take images of the same field using the green laser source.
The cells that emit both blue and green fluorescence are recognized as tumor cells.
Excite the sample with a red laser after switching sources without moving the samples.
Rotate the microscope to use the red laser.
Find cells emitting red fluorescence.
Take images of the same field using the red laser source.
Cells that emit both blue and red fluorescence are recognized as white blood cells.
Save the image obtained by each laser source.
Use ultraviolet light with an excitation plate wavelength of 330-400 nm and an emission plate wavelength of 425 nm.
Use purple light with an excitation plate wavelength of 395-415 nm and an emission plate wavelength of 455 nm.
